name: King of Tirzah
overview: The King of Tirzah was a male ruler known primarily as one of the thirty-one kings defeated by Joshua during the conquest of Canaan. The Bible does not specify his tribal affiliation or provide additional personal details. His mention is brief but significant within the context of Israel's divinely guided victories.
namesAndTitles: The title 'King of Tirzah' literally means 'king of Tirzah,' indicating his role as the monarch over the city of Tirzah. This is a straightforward title without a specific divine attribution or deeper linguistic meaning noted in Scripture.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for the King of Tirzah beyond his identification as a king defeated by Joshua. No additional relational information is provided in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: The King of Tirzah represents one of the local Canaanite rulers overcome by the Lord through Joshua's leadership, demonstrating God's faithfulness in granting Israel victory over its enemies. His defeat is part of the broader narrative of Israel's settlement in the Promised Land, highlighting God's sovereign control over the conquest process.
